updates.name: Lisa M. Marshall
updates.bio: Galveston Bay Estuary Program staff member in the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality's Water Quality Planning Division. An undated program biography describes coordinating its subcommittees on water and sediment quality and on monitoring and research, and managing the projects tied to them. Holds a University of Virginia master's in environmental science, with a hydrochemistry specialty.

No ORCID (pub.orcid.org expanded search on Lisa Marshall + Texas returned nothing). No homepage.

updates.name: Jami Belt
updates.bio: Glacier National Park biologist leading the park's Citizen Science Program since 2006 for its Crown of the Continent Research Learning Center, after earlier work at the Glacier Institute. Holds a wildlife biology master's from the University of Montana. A 2024 talk she co-presented covered citizen-science monitoring of Common Loons and Golden Eagle migration at the Mount Brown Hawk Watch.
updates.research_interests: citizen science wildlife monitoring; Common Loon monitoring; Golden Eagle migration monitoring
updates.current_title: Biologist, Citizen Science Program Manager, & Sustainability Coordinator, Crown of the Continent Research Learning Center
updates.current_affiliation: Glacier National Park, National Park Service

updates.name: Genevieve L. Noyce
updates.bio: Principal investigator leading the Smithsonian Environmental Research Center's Global Change Ecology Lab, per a 2022 SERC Q&A, and a co-principal investigator at SERC's Global Change Research Wetland. With a background in microbial ecology, she studies how warming and CO2 affect coastal wetlands in the SMARTX and GENX experiments, joining soil microbiology with biogeochemistry.
updates.research_interests: global change ecology; coastal wetland responses to warming and CO2; soil microbial ecology; biogeochemistry; soil methane emissions
updates.current_title: Principal Investigator, Global Change Ecology Lab
updates.evidence: She is also a coprincipal investigator at the center's Global Change Research Wetland
updates.notes: SERC Shorelines Q&A posted 2022-11-14 (200); the page uses she/her. SERC staff profile and lab staff pages returned 403, so no homepage. Existing ORCID checked: pub.orcid.org record name Genevieve L. Noyce, employment Smithsonian Institution (consistent). Status not set (2022 page). updates.name: Stan Rogers
updates.bio: Superintendent of Gray's Reef National Marine Sanctuary since 2019. He came from NOAA Fisheries, where he oversaw policy, planning, data and communications work at the Restoration Center and, as a senior biologist, led Endangered Species Act consultations on Navy and Defense training, after 15 years managing Air Force natural resources and conservation enforcement programs. Clemson graduate.
updates.current_affiliation: Gray's Reef National Marine Sanctuary, NOAA
updates.evidence: Stan Rogers is the superintendent at Gray's Reef National Marine Sanctuary joining the sanctuary in 2019
updates.notes: Gray's Reef staff page (200) carries a biography paragraph; it uses he. No separate profile page, so homepage left null. ORCID registry has two 'Stanley Rogers' records with no employment, so no ORCID recorded.

updates.name: Bruce A. Roundy
updates.bio: Faculty member who came to Brigham Young University in 1994 after a professorship at the University of Arizona; during his Utah State doctorate (1984) he worked as a USDA range scientist. At BYU he taught natural resources and ecology courses and received the W. R. Chapline Research Award. A fall 2018 college feature lists him among retiring faculty.

updates.name: Kelle Loughlin
updates.bio: Education coordinator at New Hampshire's Great Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve. When Phillips Exeter Academy students visited for Climate Action Day, she explained that rising seas, saltwater intrusion and shifting coastlines will force the inland estuary to adapt, and showed invasive plants growing on the Great Bay Discovery Center grounds.

Verifier: bio now ties the teaching to the one event the page describes rather than a habitual role; NH Fish and Game release returned 403 to curl but was fetched by WebFetch and names her Education Coordinator for the Great Bay NERR.

updates.name: Matthew Bernanke
updates.bio: Stewardship Coordinator (M.Sc.) at Florida's GTM Research Reserve. Wrote about, and took part in, the reserve's acoustic telemetry fieldwork, which tags scalloped hammerhead, finetooth and sandbar sharks and red drum to learn how young sharks use the estuary, a communal nursery for several shark species.
updates.research_interests: acoustic telemetry; shark nursery habitat use; scalloped hammerhead conservation
updates.current_title: Stewardship Coordinator, GTM Research Reserve / Aquatic Preserve Manager
updates.notes: Bio from 'Tracking Sharks Beneath the Surface' (Friends of the GTM Estuary Examiner, 2026; 200), bylined by him and captioning him in shark-tagging fieldwork. Florida DEP contacts page (200) gives the combined title. Existing ORCID checked: pub.orcid.org name Matthew Bernanke, employment Florida Department of Environmental Protection, Stewardship Coordinator (consistent). Verifier: removed the 'Guana Tolomato Matanzas' expansion, which the cited article does not spell out.
